description: About Me: Python AI/ML dev tackling NASA's Astronaut Health Monitoring challenge. Passionate about space tech, predictive models, & data viz. Why join: Build an AI-driven tool protecting crews from space hazards via smart health tracking. Looking For: Teammates skilled in Data Science, Space Medicine, UI/UX, or Frontend Dev!
summary:
WHAT
Astronaut Health Monitor is an autonomous health-tracking system for crews on long space missions. It records eleven indicators (heart rate, blood pressure, blood glucose, body temperature, sleep, mood, fatigue, stress, activity and radiation dose) and shows them on a web and Android dashboard with one clear answer, colour-and-symbol status and an interactive body map.

HOW
Each reading is judged against documented ranges, the astronaut's own baseline and its trend. For every out-of-range reading the app explains what to do, lists warning signs and says when to contact the flight surgeon. Machine learning flags unusual days, but documented rules always decide safety. Pulse comes from a Bluetooth sensor or a tap counter, reports can be read from a photo, and the server can run on board with no internet, so guidance never waits for Earth.

WHY
Messages to Earth can take up to 22 minutes each way, so crews must notice health changes themselves. The app gives them early warnings and clear next steps without waiting for ground control. It is an educational prototype, not a medical device.
details: WHAT IT DOES Astronaut Health Monitor helps a crew member track their own health on a long mission and know what to do next, without waiting for ground control. It records eleven indicators: heart rate, blood pressure, blood glucose, body temperature, sleep, mood, fatigue, stress, activity and radiation dose. Every reading is judged three ways: against documented safe ranges, against the astronaut's own recent baseline, and against the trend, so a slow drift is caught while values still look normal. Out-of-range readings come with causes, recommended actions, warning signs and a "contact the flight surgeon" instruction for critical values. HOW IT WORKS 1. The astronaut adds a reading by typing it, with a Bluetooth heart-rate sensor, a tap counter, a CSV file, or a photo of a printed or handwritten report (read on the device with Tesseract.js; nothing is saved until the user confirms). 2. A FastAPI server validates and stores it (SQLite or PostgreSQL, sensitive fields encrypted). 3. Documented rules decide the status: normal, caution or critical. Isolation Forest flags unusual days and linear regression forecasts risk, but machine learning only advises and never changes the safety status. 4. The dashboard shows one overall answer, at most three next steps, a card per reading, a body map with precautions per body system, and trend charts. Radiation can be typed in from a dosimeter or saved as a labelled estimate, with a running total against NASA's 600 mSv career limit. The server can run locally on board with no internet, so every reading is judged instantly. A tested offline-queue component for batch sync without duplicates is built but not yet connected to the dashboard. BENEFITS AND INTENDED IMPACT Messages to Earth can take up to 22 minutes each way. If sleep and mood slip for a week, the app flags the trend before the astronaut feels it and tells them what to do. The goal is earlier warnings and clearer next steps for crews who must act on their own. CREATIVITY Rules, personal baselines and machine learning work together in one dashboard for web and Android. Status is always a word plus a symbol, never colour alone. A clickable body map links each reading to precautions for that body system. Reports can be read from a photo on the device. FACTORS WE CONSIDERED Delayed communication and operation with no link to Earth (a local server); safety (rules decide, machine learning only advises); privacy (sign-in, encrypted health data, a tamper-evident audit log, and optional clinician and administrator roles for oversight); and honest labelling of estimated, tapped and simulated readings. VALIDITY AND QUALITY 325 automated tests with about 98% coverage, strict type checks, and a requirements document (docs/srs.md) with each requirement traced to its tests. LIMITS An educational prototype, not a medical device. Ranges come from published sources and are not clinically validated. No real crew data is included. The app cannot sense radiation itself. Bluetooth has not been tested with real sensor hardware. The Android app and browser need to reach the server; readings entered while a device is disconnected from it are not saved. TOOLS Python 3.12, FastAPI, SQLAlchemy, Pydantic, scikit-learn, pandas, NumPy, vanilla JavaScript, Tesseract.js, Android (Java), Docker and Render. LIVE DEMO (registration required) https://astro-health-8c7r.onrender.com. Choose Register, create a free account, then press "Start with sample data". The free server can take up to a minute to wake. If it is unavailable, follow the Quick start in the GitHub README to run it locally. AI ASSISTANCE Claude (Anthropic) was used as a coding assistant for code, documentation and slide text. The author set the requirements, tested the software on web and Android, reviewed the results and made the decisions.
